# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment

The verified incumbent uses 55 LUTs, 37 FFs, no DSP48s or BRAM, and meets the 10 ns `clk` constraint with setup WNS 0.494 ns and hold WHS 0.113 ns. The seed explicitly selects zero on overflow even though WIDTH-bit increment already wraps to zero; this may introduce unnecessary count-input logic and terminal-count fanout. Registered flags are required behavior, and removing dead `prev_count` alone is unlikely to save synthesized resources. Top numeric latency is UNKNOWN; leave it unannotated. Promotion requires fewer than 55 routed LUTs, nonnegative setup and hold slack, unchanged constraints, passing interface and behavioral checks, successful tool exits, exact `TEST PASSED`, `SYNTH_COMPLETE`, valid retained metrics and receipts, and evaluator ACCEPT with zero failed criteria.

## Hypothesis

Removing the explicit wrap-to-zero selection from the count datapath will reduce routed LUT usage below 55 through simpler CARRY4-based increment logic, with unchanged register count and cycle behavior.

## Instruction for generator

Inside the enabled branch, replace the conditional zero-versus-`count_next` assignments to `count` with one nonblocking WIDTH-bit increment assignment, removing the now-unused `count_next` temporary while retaining the existing conditional overflow assignments. Preserve synchronous active-high reset, reset > load > enable priority, disabled count and overflow holds, and all four flag registers updating from pre-edge `count` on every non-reset edge, including load and disabled edges. Leave threshold comparisons, parameter declarations, interface and clock unchanged; add no registers or numeric latency annotation. Validate against the unchanged independent-reference testbench, especially wrap followed by stalls, simultaneous controls, high-bit loads and threshold crossings, and review modulo arithmetic for every supported WIDTH, including WIDTH=1; retain failures and promote only after all harness gates pass.
